sentence: Given a two-digit integer \( x \), we are to find the sum of all \( x \) such that for any three-digit integer represented by \( 100a + 10b + c \) where \( x \mid (100a + 10b + c) \), it also follows that \( x \mid (100b + 10c + a) \).

- \( x \mid (100b + 10c + a) \)

x \mid \left( (100b + 10c + a) - (100a + 10b + c) \right)
\]

\]

sentence: ### Check \( x = 9 \): If \( x = 9 \), then: - Both given expressions can be divisibly by 9 without additional conditions since the digit sum divisible by 9 implies individual cycle changes satisfying symmetry transformations of digits.
